is_anopheles.evidence: The study uses female Anopheles gambiae mosquitoes for bioassays (page 4, Methods section).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper does not report genotyping of any insecticide-resistance markers. It mentions that the Kisumu strain used in the study has its kdr and ace.1R mutations controlled by PCR every 4 months (page 4), but it does not report any actual genotype data or frequencies for these markers.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No genotype data (counts or frequencies) for any insecticide-resistance markers are reported.

african_field_population.evidence: The mosquitoes used in the bioassays are from the laboratory-reared Kisumu strain (page 4, Methods section).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical study investigating the chemical composition of plant extracts and their effects on mosquitoes.

sub_country_location.evidence: The plant samples were collected from the Sebitoli forest in the northern part of the Kibale National Park, Uganda (page 4).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Plant samples were collected in 2018 and 2021 (page 4).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes new chemical analyses and bioassays.

supplement.evidence: The paper does not report any genotype data, so no supplementary genotype data is needed.

assessment.summary: This study investigates the chemical composition of essential oils from four Ugandan tree species (Vepris nobilis, Lepisanthes senegalensis, Turraeanthus africanus, and Celtis africana) and tests their repellent, irritant, and toxic effects on the laboratory-reared Kisumu strain of Anopheles gambiae. It does not report any field-collected mosquito genotype data.
exclusion_reasons: reports_target_markers: No insecticide-resistance marker genotype data reported.
african_field_population: The study uses a laboratory-reared strain (Kisumu) for bioassays, not field-collected mosquitoes.
